gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tagbanw: Raw and scattered, Disorder spaces its oversized lowercase well apart, with crossbars as fat as the stems they join. And Noto Sans Tagbanwa, a plain sans, keeps its curves open with clear gaps, so it feels tidy by comparison.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tai-vie: Disorder draws one constant stroke from top to baseline, rough and chaotic with big lowercase spaced far apart. Noto Sans Tai Viet, a sans-serif with short ascenders and pulled-back terminals, is the approachable part, and its size can stay modest.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-takri: Loud, jagged and unpolished, Disorder gives its diagonals the same heft as its stems. Noto Sans Takri, a sans with generously unclosed curves on its small round letters, steps in with a high-waisted lowercase that feels contemporary.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified even at ordinary sizes, with terminals that stop far from the stem. Disorder's heavy diagonals, matching its verticals, make the rougher partner.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tamil-s: Chaotic is the mood of Disorder, which has no hairlines anywhere and sets its glyphs well apart. But Noto Sans Tamil Supplement, a sans-serif with round forms like open parentheses and a tall middle band, does the quieter work of looking clean and stocky.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Noto Sans Tangsa reads wide and inviting, a plain sans with short ascender stems. Disorder brings a steady line with no pressure variation and a raw edge, and that tension between rough and welcoming is what makes the pair.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC reads open and approachable, a sans-serif whose tall a, e and s have large counters and outward-opening curves. And Disorder, with r, n and m arches matching their stems, adds a raw, chaotic jolt above it.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads crisp and businesslike, with a high midline. Disorder's laser-etched constant-width trace is rough, but this plain sans keeps counters connected to the outside, so paragraphs of it stay easy to move through.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Disorder is chaotic and raw, drawn at a single line weight with an oversized lowercase. Noto Sans Thaana, a plain sans, offers wide channels leading into each counter and big open lowercase forms, so it handles the quiet reading.
